How to Calculate Reselling Profit

A clear way to account for fees, shipping, item cost, and overlooked expenses.

Reselling profit is what remains after every cost tied to a sale is subtracted from the revenue you receive. The useful formula is:

Net profit = selling price − percentage fees − fixed fees − item cost − shipping − all other costs

A complete example

Suppose an item sells for $80. You paid $24, the marketplace fee is 13%, the fixed fee is $0.30, shipping costs $8.50, packaging costs $1.20, and promoted-listing cost is $2.

  • Percentage fee: $80 × 13% = $10.40
  • Total costs: $24 + $10.40 + $0.30 + $8.50 + $1.20 + $2 = $46.40
  • Estimated net profit: $80 − $46.40 = $33.60

Use the profit calculator to run the same calculation with your own numbers.

Profit is not the same as cash received

A marketplace payout may already have some fees deducted, but that payout still does not account for what you paid for the item, packing materials, repairs, mileage, or other business expenses. Record each cost once and avoid mixing personal overhead with item-level expenses unless you have a consistent allocation method.

Before listing

Calculate at the price you realistically expect to accept, not only at an optimistic list price. Then test a lower offer so you know your floor before a buyer negotiates.

Keep the estimate honest.

Fee structures and actual costs can change. Verify the rules that apply to your sale and treat every result as planning information.
